name: startup-disabled-control
description: Issue #11 control run: bandgap_core + bandgap_amp ONLY (bandgap_startup NOT instantiated), seeded at the identical degenerate .ic as sim/startup-state-search/, supply already valid (DC, not ramped), uic transient. Answers two questions: (1) is the degenerate state physically stable (not just a numerically-convenient seed)? (2) does PVT leakage alone self-start the loop at any corner without a startup circuit? This is an evidence-gathering record, not a spec-conformance claim -- contrast its per-corner iq_total_final_ua against sim/startup-state-search/'s (same seed, startup circuit present) to see the kick actually doing the work.
claim: design/bandgap_operating_point.md section 4.2's degenerate-state existence caveat -- the '(c) control run with the startup circuit disabled' leg of issue #11's required multi-pronged no-other-stable-state evidence (Implementation guidance)

vref_final_v.description: convergence sanity bound only (the point of this record is to OBSERVE where the degenerate state persists vs. self-starts via leakage, not to gate a specific outcome) -- catches a non-convergent/blown-up simulation, nothing more.
